summary:
Is it raining when and where we need it? MOODY TRENDS is an AI-assisted web platform that turns NASA Earth observation data into clear, statistically sound evidence of how the water cycle is changing. Pick any region on a 3D globe, or draw your own, and discover what is changing, where, by how much, and whether the evidence holds up, from 2001 to 2024.

We track four connected variables: precipitation, air temperature, soil moisture and evapotranspiration. Using NASA GES DISC data (GPCP, MERRA-2, GLDAS), our Python engine estimates trends per decade with OLS, HAC errors and Holm correction, and explores how variables move together without claiming causation. Results come alive in interactive maps and 3D charts, while an AI guide explains them in plain language.

It matters because Latin America and the Caribbean is the world’s largest net food-exporting region, and rainfall shifts hit harvests and livelihoods directly. MOODY TRENDS lets students, teachers and communities test “it doesn’t rain like before” against real data, and tells them honestly when the data cannot prove it.
details:
What it does

MOODY TRENDS lets anyone investigate how the water cycle is changing, without writing a line of code. The user picks a region on a 3D globe (predefined, drawn by hand, or by voice) and a period, and the platform answers four questions: what is changing, where, how much, and is it statistically significant. It tracks four linked variables from 2001 to 2024:

  • Precipitation: how much water arrives.
  • Soil moisture (0-10 cm): how much stays.
  • Air temperature: whether changes coincide with warmer conditions.
  • Actual evapotranspiration: how much returns to the atmosphere.

The 2001–2024 period was selected because it is the time range for which the dataset used provides complete information across all four variables.

How it works

  1. Data: The backend retrieves only the regional subset from NASA GES DISC via OPeNDAP: GPCP v3.3, MERRA-2 and GLDAS Noah 2.1 (288 months per variable).
  2. Processing: Units are converted once and each variable becomes one monthly value using an area- and land-weighted average, so all four describe the same territory. Missing data is flagged, never filled with zeros or interpolated.
  3. Statistics: OLS estimates change per decade, HAC (Newey-West) errors account for correlation between nearby years, and Holm correction controls false positives across the four variables. Mann-Kendall and Sen's slope serve as complementary checks.
  4. Relationships: After removing seasonality and trends, we explore correlations between variables, reporting association, never causation.
  5. Communication: Results appear as time series, anomalies, a per-pixel 3D trend map and a 3D variable network. Our AI guide, Moody, explains them in plain language by text or voice.

What makes it creative

  • A 3D globe and voice-driven exploration turn data analysis into an investigation.
  • Two paths: a guided one for beginners and an expert one with the full method visible.
  • Honest verdicts: when data cannot support a trend, we say "insufficient evidence," never "no change."
  • Moody explains results but never calculates them. All numbers come from a verified Python engine, so the AI cannot invent statistics.
  • Users can analyze their own CSV with the same method.

Factors we considered

  • Scientific validity: comparable data, autocorrelation, multiple testing, and software verified by two independent implementations plus automated tests.
  • Audience: students, teachers, technicians and community organizations, in Spanish and English, on any device, in light and dark themes.
  • Responsible scope: exploratory, not a forecast or early-warning system.

Benefits and intended impact

MOODY TRENDS makes NASA data usable for people who need it most. It helps move conversations from "it doesn't rain like before" to "what do the data show?", supporting education, evidence-based community discussion and adaptation planning. It aligns with SDG 4, 12 and 13 and with the spirit of NASA ARSET, DEVELOP and SERVIR. Next, we plan to add regions, indicators and educational activities.

Tools and technologies

  • Frontend: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn/ui
  • Visualization: react-globe.gl, three.js with react-three-fiber, Recharts
  • Backend and science: Python, FastAPI, xarray, netCDF4, statsmodels, SciPy, pymannkendall
  • AI and voice: Google Gemini, MediaRecorder, Web Speech API
  • Infrastructure: Docker, Caddy, GitHub Actions, Vercel, Microsoft Azure, GoDaddy, (no special hardware required)
